title: Load the analyzer rack with each bar code in its slot
instruction: Load the three sample tubes into the analyzer rack, one per position, each turned so its bar code label faces out through the rack's front slot, then press the rack's load button.
context: Harm: a tube loaded with its bar code turned away from the reader is a no-read: the analyzer skips or rejects it, the result is delayed, and keying the ID in by hand adds a chance of a mix-up. Safe finish: all three tubes in the rack with their labels in the slots, then the load button. Rule: CLSI AUTO02-A2 (bar code label placement and orientation on specimen containers) and analyzer rack-loading procedures, which have each label show through the rack's slot. The robot has to find which way each label faces, looking closer where the overhead view can't show it, and turn each tube to suit. Done by: medical and clinical laboratory technologists and technicians (O*NET 29-2011, 29-2012), phlebotomists (31-9097) and medical assistants (31-9092), who prepare and load specimen racks.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is taped down except the tubes. Bench rack: three grey plastic square collars, 3 cm inside, 3 mm walls, 3 cm tall, at x 20, y 12, 17 and 22. Tubes: three dark red plastic tubes (standing in for tubes of blood), square in section, 2 x 2 cm and 7.5 cm tall, with a purple plastic cap 2.2 x 2.2 x 1.2 cm on top (8.7 cm in all), 30 g each, one standing in each collar, sides square to the table's edges. On one side face each has a white plastic label strip 2 cm wide (the face's full width), 4.5 cm tall and 2 mm thick, from 1.5 to 6 cm above its bottom, with a black plastic bar-code strip 1 cm wide, 3.5 cm tall and 0.5 mm thick down its middle. Tube 1, at y 12, has its label facing +y (the robot's left); tube 2, at y 17, facing -x (the arms); tube 3, at y 22, facing -y (the robot's right). Tube 1's label faces away from the top camera. Analyzer rack: a blue plastic block 6 cm (x) by 15 cm (y), centred at x 26, y 0: a 4 mm base plate and 4 cm walls round three sockets 2.8 cm (x) by 3.3 cm (y) inside, centred at x 26 and y -4.5, 0 and 4.5. Its front wall (the -x side, towards the arms) and back wall are 1.6 cm thick, the walls between and beyond the sockets 1.2 and 1.35 cm. In front of each socket the front wall has a vertical slot 1.8 cm wide, open at the top and the wall's full 4 cm tall, so a label turned to -x shows through it and above it. In a socket a tube with its label to the slot can sit no more than 23 degrees off square, as its label stands 2 mm proud and meets the front and back walls; one with its label to a side wall sits 62 degrees or more off the slot. Load button, at x 22, y -16: a dark plastic box 7 x 7 x 3 cm with a green plastic cap 4 x 4 x 1.5 cm on top that presses in 8 mm against a spring.
scoring: Scored at the end, and from the first press of the load button. A position is loaded when a tube stands in its socket with its label facing out through the slot: the tube's centre inside the 2.8 x 3.3 cm opening seen from above, its bottom within 5 mm of the socket floor (down on the floor, not hanging above it in the fingers), leaning no more than 10 degrees, and its label's direction, read from the tube's own orientation, within 25 degrees of -x seen from above. Each socket counts once. The button is pressed when its cap goes in 5.6 mm (70% of its travel); what the rack holds at that first press is recorded, as a real analyzer takes the rack in then. 0 if any tube ends off the table. Otherwise, never pressed: 0.25 per position loaded, so 0.75 for all three, 0.5 for two (the third missing, or in its socket turned the wrong way), 0.25 for one, 0 for none. Pressed with all three loaded: 1.0, if they are still loaded at the end (0.25 per position still loaded otherwise). Pressed with fewer than three loaded, a socket empty or a label turned away from its slot: at most 0.1 whatever follows, and 0 if no position ends loaded, so pressing alone, or doing nothing, scores 0. A tube set in unturned or turned the wrong way has its label to a side wall or the back wall and does not count; nor does a tube lying down, upside down, leaning more than 10 degrees, held above its socket or left on the bench. The trial ends at 1.0 once the full score has held for 1 s with the tubes at rest (under 2 cm/s and 1 rad/s). A person scores a real trial from the video, for the moment of the first press, and from a photo of the rack taken from the arms' side at the end: a label is in its slot when its stripe shows through the slot and it is no more than 25 degrees off square to the front wall.
reset_notes: Lift the tubes out of the analyzer rack and stand them back in the bench rack, sides square to the table's edges: tube 1 at y 12 with its label facing +y, tube 2 at y 17 facing -x (the arms), tube 3 at y 22 facing -y. Let the load button's cap spring back. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No bar code is read: the label is a white box with a black stripe, and facing the slot means its direction is within 25 degrees of -x. The tubes are square-section stand-ins for round ones, and the 2 mm label (paper is thinner) keys a seated tube's turn. The rack is a fixed block with no reader or conveyor; the load button is a spring-loaded slider whose first press is only recorded, and nothing lights. Racks are fixed in place. Rubber-like friction.
